entryPoint: SLA::addGracePeriod(Datetime $date, BusinessHoursSchedule $schedule = null, &$timeline = array()) in include/class.sla.php (lines 47-65)
coreLogic: 1) Schedule precedence resolution: $schedule (requested param) ?: $this->getSchedule() (SLA's own configured schedule, lazily loaded via SLA::getScheduleId() -> BusinessHoursSchedule::lookup(), memoized on $this->_schedule) ?: $cfg->getDefaultSchedule() (system default schedule, lazily loaded via Config::getDefaultScheduleId() -> BusinessHoursSchedule::lookup(), memoized on $cfg->defaultSchedule in include/class.config.php lines 647-656). 2) If a schedule resolved, delegate to BusinessHoursSchedule::addWorkingHours($date, $this->getGracePeriod(), $timeline) in include/class.schedule.php (lines 475-484), which constructs `new BusinessHours($this)` and calls BusinessHours::addWorkingHours($date, $hours) in include/class.businesshours.php (lines 87-182) — this walks the schedule's working-hour occurrences and holiday occurrences day-by-day, advancing/backtracking $date to consume exactly $hours of business time, setting $date's timezone to the schedule's DateTimeZone, and returns false if the schedule has zero entries (getNumEntries() guard) or the input $hours is falsy/non-numeric (in which case $date is returned unchanged). BusinessHoursSchedule::addWorkingHours then copies the BusinessHours instance's internal timeline log into the by-reference $timeline param and returns $date (or false if the inner call returned false). If this whole schedule path returns truthy, SLA::addGracePeriod returns $date immediately. 3) Fallback (no schedule resolved at all, OR the schedule path returned falsy): $time = round($this->getGracePeriod()*3600); $date->add(new DateInterval('PT'.$time.'S')); return $date — a pure wall-clock addition with no business-hours/holiday awareness and no $timeline update.

Resolves $schedule = $this->getDept()->getSchedule(), builds $dt = new DateTime($this->getReopenDate() ?: $this->getCreateDate(), $tz) in the DB timezone, calls $dt = $sla->addGracePeriod($dt, $schedule), then converts $dt back to DB timezone and returns $dt->format('Y-m-d H:i:s') as the ticket's estimated SLA due date.

inputShape: $date: DateTime — the start time to advance (typically the ticket's reopen/create date, passed in the DB timezone by the only caller). $schedule: BusinessHoursSchedule|null — optional explicit schedule override; when null, resolution falls back through SLA's own schedule then the system default. &$timeline: array, by-reference, default empty array — populated with BusinessHours audit-log strings only when the schedule path executes. Implicit inputs read from object/global state: $this->getGracePeriod() (SLA's grace_period hours field), $this->getScheduleId()/getSchedule() (SLA's own schedule), global $cfg->getDefaultSchedule() (system default schedule).
outputShape: Returns the same DateTime instance passed in as $date, mutated in place (advanced by the grace period) and also returned by value; callers rely on both the mutation and the return value. addGracePeriod itself always returns a DateTime (never false/null) — an internal false from BusinessHoursSchedule::addWorkingHours (e.g. empty-schedule guard) is not propagated to the caller, it only triggers the wall-clock fallback branch which still returns $date.
sideEffects: Reads global $cfg singleton to resolve the system default schedule via $cfg->getDefaultSchedule() when no explicit/SLA schedule is available
Lazy-loads and memoizes the SLA's own schedule via SLA::getSchedule() -> BusinessHoursSchedule::lookup($this->getScheduleId()) into $this->_schedule (DB read via ORM, cached per-instance)

Config::getDefaultSchedule() lazy-loads and memoizes the system default schedule via BusinessHoursSchedule::lookup($this->getDefaultScheduleId()) into $cfg->defaultSchedule (DB read via ORM, cached on the config singleton)

When a schedule resolves, BusinessHoursSchedule::addWorkingHours() constructs a new BusinessHours($schedule) instance and calls its addWorkingHours(), which reads schedule entries and holiday schedules (getEntries(), getHolidaysSchedules()) — additional DB reads via ORM relations/lazy collections

Mutates the $date DateTime object in place in both branches: the schedule path via BusinessHours::addWorkingHours's internal $date->setTimezone()/->modify()/->sub() calls; the fallback path via $date->add($interval)

Populates the by-reference $timeline array with human-readable audit-log strings from BusinessHours::getTimeline() only when the schedule path is exercised; left as the default empty array on the fallback path
No direct DB writes occur inside addGracePeriod itself; all side effects here are reads (schedule/holiday lookups) plus in-memory caching on $this and $cfg
constraints: Schedule precedence is a strict left-to-right short-circuit: requested $schedule parameter, then $this->getSchedule() (SLA's own configured schedule), then $cfg->getDefaultSchedule() (system default) — first non-null value wins

If a schedule resolves AND BusinessHoursSchedule::addWorkingHours() returns truthy, that result is returned immediately from addGracePeriod — the wall-clock fallback below must never execute in this case

If no schedule resolves at all, OR the resolved schedule's addWorkingHours() call returns falsy (e.g. schedule has zero entries per BusinessHours::addWorkingHours's getNumEntries() guard), execution falls through to the plain-hours fallback: round(getGracePeriod()*3600) seconds added via DateInterval
Grace period hours always come from $this->getGracePeriod() (the SLA's grace_period field) — never overridable by the caller
$date is advanced in place; both branches mutate and return the same object reference, so extraction must not introduce a fresh DateTime copy that breaks caller-visible mutation
&$timeline defaults to an empty array and is only populated when the schedule branch actually runs BusinessHours::addWorkingHours; it must not be touched on the fallback branch

The schedule-path timezone side effect (setTimezone to the schedule's DateTimeZone) must be preserved exactly as-is; the fallback branch must NOT change $date's timezone, it only adds a raw DateInterval in the date's current timezone

Zero or non-numeric grace hours on the schedule path is a no-op guard inside BusinessHours::addWorkingHours (returns $date unchanged) rather than falling through to the wall-clock fallback — confirmed by the guard-zero-hours golden fixture

An empty/entry-less schedule causes BusinessHoursSchedule::addWorkingHours to return false, which must correctly fall through to the wall-clock DateInterval fallback — confirmed by the guard-empty-schedule golden fixture
harnessInputShape: JSON object with: start (string, ISO 8601 datetime); hours (number, grace period hours — use 0 for guard cases); schedule_id (integer, BusinessHoursSchedule id — 1 for normal business-hours schedule, 5 for empty-schedule fallback testing)
